full_judgment:
Md. Mozammel Hoque J: This Rule was issued directing the opposite-party No. 1 to show cause as to why judgment and decree passed by the Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 169 of 1991, affirming the judgment and decree passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 471 of 1990, decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff, should not be set-aside. 

 2. The defendant No.1 is petitioner before this court, opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted the aforesaid Title Suit for a decree for specific performance of contract in respect of the suit property. It was the case of the plaintiff that the defendant Nos. I to 4 were the owners and possessors of the suit property. The predecessor-in-interest of the defendant Nos. 1 to 4, namely, Syed Abdul Ali got this suit property on 16-3-1959 as permanent lessee from the Government in pursuance of a registered deed of lease. After the death of Syed Abdul Ali, his heirs, namely, defendant Nos. 1 to 4 inherited the suit property. The defendant Nos. 1 to 4 entered into an agreement with the plaintiff on 6-7-1993 for selling the suit property at a price of Taka 80,000.00 At the time of execution of the deed of agreement the entire consideration money was paid to the defendant Nos. 1 to 4 and it was stipulated that if within eight years the defendant could return the consideration money, the suit property would be returned to the defendants and if within the stipulated time defendants failed to return the consideration money to the plaintiff, the defendants would be bound to execute and register a deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff and on their failure, the plaintiff would be entitled to have the deed of sale executed and registered through court. It is asserted that within the stipulated time the defendant Nos. 1 to 4 failed to return the consideration money to the plaintiff and as a result the cause of action for the present suit arose on 5-8-1982. Since the defendants failed to perform their part of the contract, the plaintiff was compelled to institute the present suit for specific performance of contract 

 4. In this case the plaintiff examined four witnesses, while the defendants examined two Both the parties produced their respective papers and documents in court. On the above pleadings the trial court framed four issues. After hearing the parties and perusing the evidence on record the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka decreed the Title Suit No. 471 of 1990 in favour of the plaintiff for specific performance of contract. Against the aforesaid judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge dated 2-3-1991 the present petitioner, namely, defendant No.5 preferred an appeal before the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka being Title Appeal No. 169 of 1991. The learned Additional District Judge, after hearing the parties and perusing the materials on record, dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the learned Trial Court. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree the present petitioner namely, defendant No.5 preferred this Revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 10. Further objection was raised by the learned Deputy Attorney-General that no suit for declaring that the property in question is not an abandoned property was filed before this court. We are not concerned as to whether the plaintiff filed such a suit or not. But the present suit is a suit for specific performance of contract in pursuance of the terms and conditions as laid down in Ext. 3 the agreement of transfer. We have heard the learned Advocates, perused the materials on record and the judgments of the two courts below which considered each and every aspect of the case and we find no legal defect in the judgments of the courts below. We are of the view that the plaintiff has been able to prove the execution 'of the document, Ext. 3 as well as passing of the consideration money to the defendant Nos. 1 to 4. Since both the courts below concurrently found that this deed of agreement is a genuine document and it was duly executed by the defendant Nos. 1 to 4 and since on the basis of the material evidence on record the courts below held that the property in question could not be treated an abandoned property, we hold that the plaintiff is entitled to a decree as prayed for. We do not find any reason to interfere with the above findings of the two courts below. The learned Advocate for the petitioner failed to satisfy that there was any misconstruction of evidence or non-consideration of evidence or the court acted without jurisdiction. As such, we are of the view that the courts below have not committed any error of law occasioning any failure of justice in this case and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the courts below do not require any interference by this court. 

 11. In the result, this Rule is discharged and the judgment and decree passed by the courts below are hereby affirmed.
